turn_text: And perhaps just to add to that, can you explain a little bit the difference between the authorization and appropriations bills when it comes to defense?

Absolutely. The authorizing committee is the committee that is in charge with the policy and the authorized spending levels for certain elements of our Department of Defense. We authorize it. The appropriations committee is the committee that will actually push forward the dollars that can be spent. They will go ahead and and appropriate or allow the spending of those dollars. So I'm just going to give a random example, not based on this year's NDAA. The House and Senate Armed Services Committee will authorize a program within Department of Defense that costs $100 million. The Appropriations Committee could come back and say, yeah, that's a great program. But we're going to authorize $50 million or appropriate $50 million. And then they can only spend $50 million on that program. They don't allow the full appropriation of $100 million. So there are differences between the authorizing committees and what we feel is the right thing to do for Department of Defense, but the appropriators also have a voice in that and they may decide, well, we've only got so much money, so we're only going to appropriate X amount towards a program or the development of a platform. So there can be differences and we will push, of course, as authorizers to make sure that we're funding or appropriating the full amount
